overview: No anti-cheat consumes S35. Every corpus hit matches the TileEntity keyword rather than the packet: Grim's chunk readers and CompensatedWorld pass TileEntity arrays embedded in map-chunk data, NCP's BlockCache implementations call world.getTileEntity to read server-side block state, Kauri's BlockUpdateHandler forwards the same chunk-embedded array, Photon's WorldDownloaderSentinel writes a disable-tile-entity-saving option into the WorldDownloader channel, and intave's EntityTypeDataRegistry is a misnamed entity-type hitbox table. The only direct packet references are plumbing: Negativity's TILE_ENTITY_DATA constant, and Artemis' PacketRepository entry with the PacketPlayServerTileEntityData wrapper interface. Tile-entity policing runs on the commit side of sign edits instead: NCP AutoSign and Intave ItemCrashTracker.checkSign watch C12PacketUpdateSign, because S35 is server-trusted NBT the client applies only when the loaded tile entity matches the action byte.
